'''Gpg4win''' is an email and file encryption package for most versions of [[Microsoft Windows]] and [[Microsoft Outlook]], which utilises the [[GnuPG]] framework for [[symmetric encryption|symmetric]] and [[public-key cryptography]], such as data encryption, [[digital signature]]s, [[Cryptographic hash function|hash calculations]] etc.

== History of Gpg4win ==
The original creation of Gpg4win was initiated and funded by Germany's [[Federal Office for Information Security]] (BSI) in 2005,<ref>{{Cite web |date=2009-08-14 |title=Gpg4win - Email-Security using GnuPG for Windows |url=http://www.gpg4win.org/change-history.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090814032737/http://www.gpg4win.org/change-history.html |archive-date=2009-08-14  |access-date=2022-09-14 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Hillenius |first=Gijs |date=19 December 2013 |title=Government-used cryptography tool seeks funds |url=https://joinup.ec.europa.eu/news/government-used-cryptography |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180119120207/https://joinup.ec.europa.eu/news/government-used-cryptography |access-date=25 April 2019 |archive-date=2018-01-19 |via=europa.eu |quote=Germany's Federal Office for Information Security (BSI)…in 2006…funded the development of GPG4win}}</ref> resulting in the release of Gpg4win 1.0.0 on 6 April 2006;<ref>{{cite web |url=https://files.gpg4win.org/ |quote=Timestamp of installer file `gpg4win-1.0.0.exe`: 06 April 2006 |via=gpg4win.org |title=About Gpg4win |date=6 April 2006 |access-date=6 January 2022 }}</ref> however Gpg4win and all included tools are [[free and open source software]], and it is typically the non-proprietary option for privacy recommended<ref>{{cite news |url=https://arstechnica.com/information-technology/2013/06/encrypted-e-mail-how-much-annoyance-will-you-tolerate-to-keep-the-nsa-away/ |title=Encrypted e-mail: How much annoyance will you tolerate to keep the NSA away?|first1=Peter |last1=Bright |first2=Dan |last2=Goodin |date=14 June 2013 |work=[[Ars Technica]] |access-date=25 April 2019 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.pcworld.com/article/245534/gpg4win_powerful_encryption_for_free.html |title=Gpg4win: Powerful Encryption for Free |first=Erez |last=Zukerman |work=[[PCWorld]] |date=5 December 2011 |access-date=25 April 2019 |archive-date=30 May 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140530181916/http://www.pcworld.com/article/245534/gpg4win_powerful_encryption_for_free.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> to Windows users.

As Gpg4win v1 was a much overhauled derivate of GnuPP,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.gnupp.com/start.html |title=GnuPP project |date=May 2002 |access-date=6 January 2022 }}</ref> both were using [[GnuPG#Branches|GnuPG v1]] for cryptographic operations and thus only supported [[OpenPGP]] as cryptography standard.

Hence in 2007 the development of a fundamentally enhanced version was started, also with support from the German BSI ([[Federal Office for Information Security]]); this effort culminated in the release of Gpg4win 2.0.0 on 7 August 2009 after a protracted beta testing phase,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://gpg4win.org/news-20090812.html |title=Gpg4win 2.0.0 press release |quote=Press release: Gpg4win 2.0.0 is ready, it does S/MIME and secure attachments |via=gpg4win.org |date=2009-08-12 |access-date=6 January 2022 }}</ref> which was based on GnuPG 2.0, included [[S/MIME]] support, Kleopatra as a new certificate manager, the [[Windows Explorer|Explorer]] plug-in GpgEX for cryptography operations on files, basic support of [[smart card]]s, a full set of German dialogue texts in addition to the English ones, new manuals in English and German, plus many other enhancements.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://files.gpg4win.org/README-2.0.0.en.txt |title=README-2.0.0.en.txt |via=gpg4win.org |date=2009-08-07 |access-date=6 January 2022 }}</ref>

In contrast to Gpg4win v2, which focused on new features and software components, the development of Gpg4win v3 focused on usability, plus consolidation of code and features:<ref>{{cite web |url=https://gpg4win.org/version3.html |title=What's new in Gpg4win 3? |via=gpg4win.org |date=20 September 2017 |access-date=6 January 2022 }}</ref> This resulted in the release of Gpg4win 3.0.0 on 19 September 2017 with proper support for [[Elliptic Curve Cryptography|Elliptic Curve Cryptography (ECC)]] by utilising GnuPG 2.2 (instead of 2.0), broadened, stabilised and enhanced smart card support, a fundamentally overhauled [[Microsoft Outlook|Outlook]] plug-in GpgOL for Outlook 2010 and newer, support of 64-bit versions of Outlook 2010 and newer, supporting dialogues in all languages which KDE supports etc.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://files.gpg4win.org/README-3.0.0.en.txt |title=README-3.0.0.en.txt |via=gpg4win.org |date=19 September 2017 |access-date=6 January 2022 }}</ref> It is also distributed as GnuPG VS-Desktop with commercial support and approval for handling [[Classified information#NATO classifications|NATO RESTRICTED]], [[Classified information#International organizations|RESTREINT UE/EU RESTRICTED]] and [[Classified information#Table of equivalent classification markings in various countries|German VS-NfD]] documents, which in turn has become the major source of revenue for maintaining and further developing the GnuPG framework and Gpg4win.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://gnupg.org/blog/20220102-a-new-future-for-gnupg.html |title=A New Future for GnuPG |via=gnupg.org |date=2 January 2022 |access-date=6 January 2022 }}</ref>

Gpg4win 4.0.0, released on 21 December 2021,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://files.gpg4win.org/README-4.0.0.en.txt |title=README-4.0.0.en.txt |via=gpg4win.org |date=12 December 2017 |access-date=6 January 2022 }}</ref> switched to using GnuPG 2.3 (from 2.2) and continued to refine and enhance the feature set of Gpg4win v3.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://gpg4win.org/version4.html |title=What's new in Gpg4win 4? |via=gpg4win.org |date=12 December 2021 |access-date=6 January 2022 }}</ref>

== Contents of Gpg4win Installer ==
* [[GnuPG]]: the core cryptography framework
* Certificate managers
** Kleopatra: certificate manager for OpenPGP and X.509 
** GPA: an alternative certificate manager ([[GNU]]) for OpenPGP and X.509
* Plug-ins for email and file cryptography
** GpgOL: a plug-in for [[Microsoft Outlook]] to provide [[email encryption]] and signing
** GpgEX: a plug-in for the [[Windows Explorer]] to provide file encryption, signing and hash calculations
* ''Gpg4win Compendium'': an introduction to encryption (OpenPGP and [[X.509]]) and user manual for Gpg4win
